Actor.description:
Who performed a change (§17). `authorized_by` is DERIVED from the matching approval stamp,
never trusted from the YAML, so an `importer` actor cannot authorise its own promotion.
Actor.title: Actor

ApprovalAction.description: The closed sub-approval catalog (§13). Each action has one legal target record kind.
ApprovalAction.title: ApprovalAction

ApprovalEntry.description:
One owner decision inside the revision's single stamp (§13).

`target_content_digest` is the canonical digest of the target record BEFORE any approval
metadata is attached, which is what makes the binding acyclic and what makes a post-approval
edit detectable.
ApprovalEntry.title: ApprovalEntry

ApprovalLedger.description: `history/approvals.yaml`. One stamp per promoted revision, in promotion order.
ApprovalLedger.title: ApprovalLedger

ApprovalStamp.description:
One promoted revision appends exactly one stamp, which may carry any number of entries (§13).

`entries` may be empty: the stamp itself authorizes the candidate revision, so a revision whose
diff triggers no sub-approval needs none. An empty list is therefore a legitimate state, not a
missing approval.
ApprovalStamp.title: ApprovalStamp

ApprovedVia.description:
How the owner confirmed. One member today, and it is the seam: adding a second is a visible
schema decision rather than a free-text string a caller can invent.
ApprovedVia.title: ApprovedVia

AssertionAuthorizationBranch.description:
One complete authorization route for a tag (§15).

Exactly the four fields the design declares, all required. Within one branch every non-empty
constraint is ANDed; items inside either list are alternatives. At least one constraint must be
set, or the branch would authorize the tag unconditionally — which is how `production` would
become claimable about a merely `completed` project.
AssertionAuthorizationBranch.title: AssertionAuthorizationBranch

BlobCapture.description:
A larger capture stored once under `blobs/sha256/`.

`sha256` is the bare raw-byte digest of the POST-redaction bytes. The filesystem path is never
an identity input, which is what lets a bundle be relocated for encrypted backup.
BlobCapture.title: BlobCapture

CandidateOccurrence.description:
One (source snapshot, normalised record bytes) sighting of a candidate value.

Re-enumerating changed source bytes at the same locator APPENDS an occurrence rather than
replacing prior lineage, so the history of where a value was seen survives a source edit.
CandidateOccurrence.title: CandidateOccurrence

CandidateRecord.description: One typed candidate assertion with its append-only occurrences (§18).
CandidateRecord.title: CandidateRecord

CaptureMediaType.description:
The initial capture media allowlist (§12.2). Closed — no other media is accepted.

It lives with the record shape it constrains rather than with the scanner that reads it, so the
models package stays importable without the scanner and there is no import cycle between them.
Other media require a later reviewed design, because "scan it as UTF-8 text" is the only
inspection this phase implements.
CaptureMediaType.title: CaptureMediaType

Cardinality.description: How many EFFECTIVE facts a subject may carry for this predicate (§10.4).
Cardinality.title: Cardinality

CaveatSeverity.description:
A `context_required` caveat must travel with any later projection of the figure; a
`disqualifying` one makes the metric ineligible until a new metric supersedes it (§11).
CaveatSeverity.title: CaveatSeverity

ChangeLedger.description:
`history/changes.yaml`. Append-only, and contiguous from revision 1.

A gap would make "change-ledger length equals the revision number" unenforceable, which is the
cheap check that catches a rewritten history without recomputing every ancestor.
ChangeLedger.title: ChangeLedger

ChangeRecord.description:
One promoted revision's change record (§17).

The resulting bundle digest deliberately lives only in the manifest: putting it here would make
the change record contain a hash of a document containing the change record.

`changed_record_ids` is derived by the authoring CLI from the validated draft diff rather than
trusted from a manually authored list, which is why nothing downstream treats it as authority
for what actually changed — the record digests do.
ChangeRecord.title: ChangeRecord

ClaimRecord.description:
One approved-or-proposed wording (§15).

`required_fact_ids` may be empty at parse time: "an approved claim must reference at least one
fact" is status-dependent, so enforcing it intrinsically would make a `draft` claim
unrepresentable while the owner is still assembling its support.

Every required record is *conjunctive* support for the complete wording, which is why §10.3
makes claim surfaces a subset of the INTERSECTION of all required facts' and metrics' surfaces
rather than the union.
ClaimRecord.title: ClaimRecord

ClaimType.description:
The closed initial claim-type catalog (§15).

The first three live in `claims/bullet-candidates.yaml`; `professional_summary` lives only in
`claims/summary-candidates.yaml`. A type in the wrong file is a hard validation failure, which
is what stops a summary from being selected as a bullet.
ClaimType.title: ClaimType

ConflictRecord.description:
One group of competing otherwise-effective values for one subject and predicate (§13).

At least two candidates: a "conflict" with one candidate has nothing to choose between, and
admitting it would let a fact be parked in a permanently unresolved group to dodge cardinality.
ConflictRecord.title: ConflictRecord

ConflictRulings.description: `conflicts/rulings.yaml`. Append-only: promotion requires the parent sequence as a prefix.
ConflictRulings.title: ConflictRulings

ConflictState.description:
`reopened` exists because new evidence must be able to reopen a settled group without
deleting the ruling that settled it (§13).
ConflictState.title: ConflictState

ContactRecord.description:
One typed contact channel on the single `person` entity (§9).

Contact values and their surfaces require a `confirm_contact` sub-approval in the revision's
approval stamp; a `verification_state` of `owner_confirmed` in the YAML alone establishes
nothing.
ContactRecord.title: ContactRecord

DateRangeValue.description:
A closed range, or an open one with `end: null`.

Ordering is not enforced here. §10.4 declares "start <= end" as `employment.date_range`'s and
`affiliation.date_range`'s exclusivity rule, so enforcing it intrinsically would apply it to
predicates whose catalog row does not ask for it.
DateRangeValue.title: DateRangeValue

DeferralModel.description:
A locator that deliberately matches no producing rule and carries a specific drain reason
(extraction.py `Deferral`).
DeferralModel.title: DeferralModel

Disposition.description:
Every enumerated record gets exactly one (§18). `review_required` is a Gate B blocker:
an undispositioned record is the "unexplained record" the gate requires to be zero.
Disposition.title: Disposition

DraftManifest.description:
A writable draft. Has no `revision`, `created_at`, or `created_by` — promotion derives them.

`draft_of_revision` and `parent_bundle_digest` are null together for the revision-1 draft `init`
creates, and non-null together for every `checkout`. A half-set pair would make "is this
parentless?" answerable two ways.
DraftManifest.title: DraftManifest

EmploymentFactsDocument.description: `facts/experience/<employment-id>.yaml`: exactly one employment entity and its facts.
EmploymentFactsDocument.title: EmploymentFactsDocument

EntryKindModelEntry.description: One entry kind, keyed by its inner `kind` field (extraction.py `EntryKindSpec`).
EntryKindModelEntry.title: EntryKindModelEntry

EvidenceAlternative.description:
One independently sufficient way to meet a predicate's minimum evidence standard.

§10.4: "Each listed minimum evidence class is independently sufficient unless the entry lists a
combination." An alternative is therefore a set of classes that must ALL be present, and a
predicate lists one alternative per acceptable route.
EvidenceAlternative.title: EvidenceAlternative

EvidenceRecordsDocument.description:
`evidence/records.yaml`. §7 step 2 reads evidence records ONLY from here, which is what makes
the evidence-set digest a function of one document plus the blob bytes it names.
EvidenceRecordsDocument.title: EvidenceRecordsDocument

ExclusionRecord.description:
One excluded source record and why (§18). Every exclusion requires a rationale.

`owner_excluded` additionally requires an `approve_source_record_exclusion` sub-approval bound
to the excluded record's target-content digest — a graph check, since it needs the stamp.
ExclusionRecord.title: ExclusionRecord

ExclusivitySpec.description:
The closed exclusivity rules the design's catalog actually uses (§10.4).

`NONE` is an explicit rule rather than an omission. `ONE_EFFECTIVE_RANGE_ORDERED` carries both
halves of the design's "one effective range; start <= end" cell, because splitting them would
let a row ask for the ordering without the uniqueness or the reverse.
ExclusivitySpec.title: ExclusivitySpec

ExpirySpec.description:
The design's "Expiry; review" cell, both halves explicit.

`review_interval_days: null` is the design's `null` review column — no fixed interval — and is
a required key so "we decided there is no interval" appears in the diff.
ExpirySpec.title: ExpirySpec

ExtractionMappingsDocument.description:
`policy/extraction-mappings.yaml`.

Seeded NON-EMPTY (a version plus the one resume adapter): unlike the enumeration-owned import
documents, the extraction mapping is build-supplied catalog content written into the revision so
a bundle's extraction behaviour is fixed by its own rows.
ExtractionMappingsDocument.title: ExtractionMappingsDocument

ExtractionReport.description:
`imports/extraction-report.yaml`.

Keyed by `source_record_id` and bound into the candidate digest, it explains every
`review_required` record without asserting disposition (§6.3a). A fresh bundle has no sources,
so the seed is empty.
ExtractionReport.title: ExtractionReport

ExtractionReportEntry.description: One `review_required` record and the closed reason it stays unresolved (§6.3a).
ExtractionReportEntry.title: ExtractionReportEntry

ExtractionReportReason.description:
The closed reasons a `review_required` record stays unresolved (§6.3a).

The report is the drain's durable carrier: exactly one reason is attached to every
`review_required` record, and none to an `imported` or `excluded` one. It explains the resulting
unresolved state and never asserts a disposition — disposition stays derived from candidates and
exclusions. Out-of-catalog is a failure, never a new bucket.
ExtractionReportReason.title: ExtractionReportReason

FactRecord.description:
One atomic assertion (§10).

`supersedes_fact_ids` is an edge, not a mutation: a corrected fact gets a NEW `fact_id` and the
superseded record stays immutable, so history is derivable rather than overwritten. That is
also why a correction cannot break cardinality — cardinality counts effective facts only.
FactRecord.title: FactRecord

FactValueKind.description: The closed initial value union (§10.1). A new kind bumps `schema_version`.
FactValueKind.title: FactValueKind

GatedFactsDocument.description:
`application/gated-facts.yaml` (§16).

Professional facts that may be needed for an application but must never reach a résumé or a
public artefact. The surface restriction is intrinsic to the file: a record here declaring
`resume` would be an application-only fact widening itself — the exact leak §10.3's graph
invariants exist to prevent — and the file-level check catches it before any graph is built.
GatedFactsDocument.title: GatedFactsDocument

IdentityDocument.description: `facts/identity.yaml`: the one person entity, its contact channels, and its facts.
IdentityDocument.title: IdentityDocument

ImportLineage.description:
Where an imported fact came from. Provenance only: §18 makes upstream sources historical
after baseline promotion, and nothing downstream may resolve `source_locator` to read them.
ImportLineage.title: ImportLineage

InlineCapture.description:
A small capture stored directly in `evidence/records.yaml`.

Inline text contributes to identity through the normalised evidence document and has no
separate blob leaf, so two records quoting the same excerpt do not deduplicate.
InlineCapture.title: InlineCapture

LocalSourcesSidecar.description: Logical source ID -> machine-local absolute root. Nothing else is representable.
LocalSourcesSidecar.title: LocalSourcesSidecar

Locator.description:
Where inside the origin the capture came from.

The design declares no closed locator-kind catalog, so `kind` is an open lowercase token rather
than an invented enum: a fabricated catalog would reject legitimate authoring (a page range, a
heading path, a cell reference) with no design authority behind the refusal.
Locator.title: Locator

MetricCaveat.description: A typed caveat. Severity is enforced; the text is for the human reading the projection.
MetricCaveat.title: MetricCaveat

MetricQualifier.description: How exactly the number should be read (§11).
MetricQualifier.title: MetricQualifier

MetricRecord.description:
One measured claim about one subject (§11).

`allowed_phrasings` is non-empty by contract — §11 requires "at least one allowed phrasing"
before a metric can be considered for a future résumé — and `evidence_ids` is non-empty because
a metric with no evidence is a number somebody remembered.

`protected_tokens` may be empty: §15 cross-checks "any rendered protected metric tokens", so a
metric that declares none simply has nothing to preserve. It is a required key rather than a
defaulted one, so "we decided there are none" is visible in the diff.
MetricRecord.title: MetricRecord

MetricRendering.description:
How a referenced metric appears in the claim text.

§15 names `qualitative_only` explicitly and requires it for "a referenced metric omitted from
the text". A metric whose figure DOES appear needs a value too, and `rendered` is that value:
the enum must have two members or the distinction the design draws is unrepresentable. The
inference is recorded here rather than buried, because a third rendering would be a schema bump.
MetricRendering.title: MetricRendering

MetricValue.description:
The number, its unit key, and its qualifier.

`number` is a decimal string, never a float: `0.1` has no exact binary form, so two writers
could serialise the same measurement differently and the bundle digest would disagree.
`unit` is a key into the revision-owned `policy/units.yaml`; closure is checked semantically.
MetricValue.title: MetricValue

ModelRoutedRuleModel.description:
A rule whose predicate and value come from the entry_kind_model (extraction.py
`ModelRoutedRule`).
ModelRoutedRuleModel.title: ModelRoutedRuleModel

OwnerAttestationAuthority.description:
What state, if any, owner attestation alone may establish (§10.4).

Every initial predicate that admits owner attestation uses `owner_confirmed`, never `verified`.
`VERIFIED` exists because the design declares the catalog as
`none | verified | owner_confirmed`; a test asserts no shipped row uses it.
OwnerAttestationAuthority.title: OwnerAttestationAuthority

OwnerAttestationEvidence.description:
An owner attestation needs `attested_at` and at least one supported fact.

That the supported fact is `owner_confirmed` and carries a `confirm_fact` sub-approval is a
graph property, checked in semantic validation: it needs the fact record and the stamp.
OwnerAttestationEvidence.title: OwnerAttestationEvidence

PortableOrigin.description:
A public record's origin, expressed portably.

One `reference` field rather than a url/citation pair: §12 requires the origin be *portable*,
and validation rejects absolute personal paths in it. Two optional fields would let a record
satisfy the contract with neither filled in.
PortableOrigin.title: PortableOrigin

PredicateCatalog.description:
`policy/predicates.yaml`.

The document version and every entry's `catalog_version` must agree: §10.1 puts the version on
the entry, and the manifest carries `predicate_catalog_version`. Three copies of one number is
only safe if disagreement is an error, so it is.
PredicateCatalog.title: PredicateCatalog

PredicateSpec.description:
One predicate contract (§10.1, §10.4). No field has a parser default.

`legal_string_values` carries the design's one enumerated value cell:
`deployment.environment`'s value type is "string enum: development, staging, production".
Representing it as data is what makes that enum enforceable instead of decorative — §21 lists
an unknown enum as a hard failure, and §15's `production` tag authorization requires the value
to be exactly `production`. An empty tuple means "unconstrained beyond the value type", and
every row must state it explicitly.
PredicateSpec.title: PredicateSpec

ProjectFactsDocument.description: `facts/projects/<project-id>.yaml`: exactly one project entity and its facts.
ProjectFactsDocument.title: ProjectFactsDocument

Redaction.description:
One removed region over the UTF-8 bytes of the stored post-redaction capture (§12.2).

Half-open `[start, end)`. The range must contain exactly the ASCII marker
`[REDACTED:<reason>]`, so the validator can verify every recorded redaction against retained
bytes without ever storing what was removed. Multiple removed regions therefore need multiple
markers and multiple entries.
Redaction.title: Redaction

RelationRecord.description:
One typed edge between two entities.

`relation_type` is a catalog key, not a code enum: §9 puts the relation catalog in
`policy/relations.yaml` as versioned revision data, and the legal source/target entity kinds
are declared there. Semantic validation checks this record against that catalog.
RelationRecord.title: RelationRecord

RelationSpec.description: One relation type and the entity kinds its endpoints may name (§9).
RelationSpec.title: RelationSpec

RepositoryArtifactEvidence.description:
A repository artifact needs the FULL commit, not an abbreviated one.

An abbreviation is ambiguous across a repository's lifetime, so it cannot identify the bytes
the capture was taken from — which is the only thing that makes the capture re-checkable.
RepositoryArtifactEvidence.title: RepositoryArtifactEvidence

RevisionManifest.description:
One immutable promoted revision (§7).

`parent_bundle_digest` is required after revision 1, which is what makes local history explicit
without depending on Git. Revision directories are named by `bundle_digest`; the revision NUMBER
never appears in a directory name, so two torn attempts at the same content cannot reserve two
numbered slots.
RevisionManifest.title: RevisionManifest

RulingRecord.description:
One append-only owner decision about a conflict (§13).

`select_candidate` names the winner; every other decision must not, because a `keep_unresolved`
or `not_applicable` ruling that also selected a fact would make the group both undecided and
decided.
RulingRecord.title: RulingRecord

SecondarySummaryEvidence.description:
Import evidence, not final verification.

`authoritative` is `Literal[False]`: §12 makes a secondary summary non-authoritative unless a
predicate contract explicitly permits it, so a `true` here would be a contradiction in terms
rather than a stronger claim.
SecondarySummaryEvidence.title: SecondarySummaryEvidence

SecretRule.description:
One named detection rule: exactly `rule_id`, `pattern`, and `flags` (§12.2).

`pattern` is compiled at construction time so an unparseable regex is rejected where it is
authored, rather than surfacing later as an opaque `re.error` from inside a scan — which would
make a capture unscannable while looking like a clean one.
SecretRule.title: SecretRule

SecretRuleset.description:
`policy/secret-scan.yaml`: `ruleset_version` plus `rules`, and nothing else (§12.2).

The row shape lives here with the other catalogs; the built-in v1 registry and the scanning
itself live in `secret_scan`, which is where the rules are applied.
SecretRuleset.title: SecretRuleset

SecretScanFlag.description: The closed set of `re` behaviours a rule may opt into (§12.2). Nothing else parses.
SecretScanFlag.title: SecretScanFlag

SelectedSectionsScope.description:
A repository-Markdown source's approved scope.

`locators` is a non-empty, order-preserving list of normalised heading paths. Order is preserved
because widening or reordering the approved scope changes the `approve_source_scope` target
digest, which is the whole point: a scope change must cost a new owner approval.
SelectedSectionsScope.title: SelectedSectionsScope

SkillCategoryCatalog.description:
`policy/skill-categories.yaml`: field-dependent taxonomy, never a code vocabulary (§10.4).

`career_field` is part of the catalog so a bundle states which field its categories belong to.
Gate A uses a synthetic catalog; Gate B gathers the private one for the user's declared field.
SkillCategoryCatalog.title: SkillCategoryCatalog

SkillCategorySpec.description: One skill category. `parent_category_id` is optional per §10.4 and defaults to `null`.
SkillCategorySpec.title: SkillCategorySpec

SkillRecord.description:
One canonical capability.

`category` is a key into the revision-owned `policy/skill-categories.yaml` catalog, never a
code-defined software vocabulary: §10.4 makes categories field-dependent data so the mechanism
fits a user whose career has nothing to do with software.

`allowed_surfaces` must be a subset of the union of its eligible supporting facts' surfaces
(§10.3). That is a graph invariant checked in semantic validation, because it needs the facts.
SkillRecord.title: SkillRecord

SlotModel.description:
One fully specified emission of an entry-kind model (extraction.py `Slot`).

`value_from` is a scalar field name (or `.`), or an O3c coalesce priority list. The union parses
a YAML scalar to a `str` and a YAML list to a `tuple`, matching the interpreter's dataclass.
SlotModel.title: SlotModel

SourceKind.description: The closed source-kind catalog (§18). Each pairs with exactly one approved enumerator.
SourceKind.title: SourceKind

SourceLedgerRecord.description: One deterministically enumerated source record — one unit of the Gate B denominator.
SourceLedgerRecord.title: SourceLedgerRecord

SourceLedgerSource.description:
One enumerated source's ledger entry (§18).

Owns only enumeration, scope, digest, and record state. `source_kind` and `portable_locator`
live in `policy/sources.yaml` and are deliberately not repeated here — two homes for one field
is two chances to disagree.
SourceLedgerSource.title: SourceLedgerSource

SourceSpec.description:
Portable source metadata only (§6, §18).

`policy/sources.yaml` is authoritative for `source_kind` and `portable_locator`;
`imports/source-ledger.yaml` owns enumeration, scope, digests, and dispositions. The two
documents may not repeat the same metadata fields, so there is no `enumerator_id` here.

Absolute machine-local roots live only in the non-revisioned root `local-sources.yaml`, which
is why `portable_locator` is relative. The field validator below is where that lands: it
refuses an absolute path, a drive qualifier, a backslash, a `.`/`..` component, a control
character, and a leading `~`. Nothing else in `validation/` reads this field — the personal-path
scan walks evidence records only — so a claim about it that is not in that validator is false.
SourceSpec.title: SourceSpec

StringListValue.description:
An ordered list. §18 sorts *set-like* candidate lists by canonical identity; a value that is
genuinely a sequence keeps its order, so `values` rejects duplicates without reordering.
StringListValue.title: StringListValue

SufficiencyState.description:
Whether an owner has reviewed the capture for sufficiency (§12).

`owner_approved` must match an approval-stamp sub-entry bound to this record's target-content
digest. The record embeds no approval ID, which is what keeps that binding acyclic.
SufficiencyState.title: SufficiencyState

Surface.description: Where a record may be projected. Internal storage is implicit and is not a surface.
Surface.title: Surface

SurfacePolicy.description:
`application_only` forbids `resume` and `public` even if a future catalog edit accidentally
widens `legal_surfaces` (§10.4). It is a second, independent latch on the same door.
SurfacePolicy.title: SurfacePolicy

UnitCatalog.description: `policy/units.yaml`. Gate A ships no universal built-in unit vocabulary (§11).
UnitCatalog.title: UnitCatalog

UnitSpec.description:
Exactly the five columns §11 declares. Nothing else is a unit's business.

The catalog defines no conversions, implicit aliases, or dimensional inference: validation does
exact ID/alias lookup only, so `120 ms` can never be silently compared with `0.12 s`.
UnitSpec.title: UnitSpec

UsageContext.description:
How the subject used or encountered the material (§10.1).

Context does not change evidence strength. `incidental` can never ground a verified skill.
UsageContext.title: UsageContext

VerificationState.description:
The closed fact-state catalog (§10.2).

`owner_confirmed` is not a weaker synonym for `verified`: predicate contracts say when owner
attestation is the appropriate authority, and it can never prove a repository implementation,
a publication, or a measured result.
VerificationState.title: VerificationState

description:
A synthetic root whose only purpose is to pull every document model into one `$defs` block.

Nothing constructs it. The alternative — one schema file per document — would give an authoring
agent thirty-three files to fetch and no single place to see the whole contract.
title: boardwatch career-profile bundle
